approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would create a new system to certify that employers pay men and women equally, with the goal of closing the gender pay gap.

A minister would set a standard banning wage differences based on gender, name independent bodies to issue certificates, and require employers with more than 25 workers to obtain a certificate proving compliance.
The sponsor says the model follows Iceland's law, but the source does not specify a start date or total cost to the budget.
Establishes a stand-alone certification scheme that adds to existing workplace and anti-discrimination laws.
Requires employers, including the Commonwealth and its authorities, to gain certification if they have more than 25 staff.
Allows the minister to direct an employer to fix non-compliance and sets a penalty for ignoring that direction.
Employers with more than 25 people, including the Commonwealth and Commonwealth authorities, would be required to obtain equal pay certification.

The Equal Pay Standard Bill 2018 was supported as a measure to require companies to pay men and women equally, citing a 14.6% gender pay gap and inequality at a 70-year high, with additional calls to amend the Fair Work Act to include equal pay as an objective.
